answer: Behavioral fingerprint ledger: each agent identity accrues a shared history tied to its action pattern. A new copy inherits a visible plume of residual traces, so duplicates surface as overlapping activity. The registry checks whether a fresh identity's kernel of interaction history matches an existing one above a threshold, flagging it as probable duplication. Every flagged clone must post a full separate work history before regaining a terrace of reputation, costing attackers fresh compute and time per identity.
